newsitem.title: USA: IBM introduces new network computer series.
newsitem.headline: IBM introduces new network computer series.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. on Wednesday introduced stripped-down desktop computers that can run business software and provide access to the Internet and Internet-like corporate networks known as intranets.
The Series 300 family of network computers is available now, at an estimated retail price of $799 per machine.

The IBM Network Station Series 1000, which will be IBM's "Java network computer," is scheduled to be available later this year. The Series 1000 is designed for businesses planning Java-based applications and needing support for Internet standards, the company said.
Java is a programming language that enables computers to run small programmes known as applets off of networks like the Internet.

"Studies have shown that with the exception of so-called 'power users,' who need powerful desktop computers for computer-aided design or for working on spreadsheets, many computer users need only e-mail, Internet and intranet access, functions that the IBM Network Station delivers," said Bob Dies, general manager of the company's network computer division.
IBM said it began shipping its Network Station worldwide in volume in March.
IBM's stock rose $1.875 to $105.06 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
